novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new measurement decomposition and associated mechanistic comparison: “multilingual factual inconsistency has two additive components,” with a “language-specific residual” separated from within-language paraphrase instability, rather than merely applying a standard tool to another language. The closest prior work I located, *Lost in Multilinguality: Dissecting Cross-lingual Factual Inconsistency in Transformer Language Models* (ACL 2025), attributes failures to a late-layer language transition, while *Cross-Lingual Consistency of Factual Knowledge in Multilingual Language Models* (EMNLP 2023) measures cross-lingual inconsistency without this paraphrase-controlled baseline; searches using “cross-lingual inconsistency paraphrase instability,” “paraphrase-controlled cross-lingual consistency,” “language transition residual multilingual factuality,” and “within-language paraphrase variability multilingual QA” did not identify an essentially equivalent study. The step from these works to the claim is a non-trivial combination and operationalization of paraphrase robustness with mechanistic cross-lingual localization—more than a direct object transfer, but still a natural extension of existing questions rather than a new core paradigm—so it fits the 5–6 band.
